findings.root_cause:
CUDA 13 changed the <<<>>> ABI. Without __NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH, the host stub fetches a cudaKernel_t once through __cudaGetKernel and passes that handle to __cudaLaunchKernel, which tail-branches into cudaLaunchKernel. The handle is a heap object; cudaKernel_t is typedef struct CUkern_st*, the same type as CUkernel (driver_types.h:3239, cuda.h:293).

bpftime identifies launches by host-stub address, and all three of its routes fail:
(1) The registration map is empty in preload and attach mode.
(2) The late path names the pointer through dladdr and the ELF symbol cache. For an address outside every module, resolve_host_function_symbol returns the nearest lower symbol, because it skips the end check for size-0 entries (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1670). The result is a meaningless name (__end__ here, _fini in #646) that matches no patched kernel.
(3) The driver-level replacement names its argument only with cuFuncGetName (frida_setup.cpp:459-466), which rejects CUkernel handles with 400. The helper that would work, cuda_graph_maybe_get_kernel_name_from_cukernel (:473-487), exists but only the graph hooks use it (:607-609).

Every miss is logged at DEBUG, so at the default level the run looks successful.
findings.fix_sketch:
Smallest fix, at the runtime level. It covers cudaLaunchKernel and cudaLaunchKernel_ptsz, which share cuda_launch_kernel_common (frida_setup.cpp:550-571).

(a) Before the late-path resolver at frida_setup.cpp:203, classify the pointer. If dladdr(func) finds no containing object, it cannot be a host stub, so treat it as a cudaKernel_t and name it with the existing cuda_graph_maybe_get_kernel_name_from_cukernel((CUkernel)func). Otherwise keep resolve_host_function_symbol. Cache the pointer->name result, positive and negative, so dladdr and cuKernelGetName run once per pointer. The existing redirect and fallback to the original (:205-235) stay as they are.

(b) Harden the resolver:
- nv_attach_impl.cpp:1670-1673: reject a size-0 entry unless needle == it->start.
- nv_elf_introspect.cpp:161: skip names starting with '$' (AArch64 mapping symbols).
- Sort equal starts with sized entries last, so upper_bound-1 picks the sized symbol.

(c) Log with BPFTIME_LOG_WARN_RATELIMITED when a launch pointer cannot be named at all, so a miss shows at the default level.

(d) Required companion, shared with F6. When mirror_cuda_memcpy_to_symbol cannot map a write (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1299-1300 and 1360-1361), set a flag and stop redirecting, with a WARN. Otherwise stripped default-flag binaries would now run patched kernels on stale __constant__ data.

Alternative, not preferred: in cu_launch_kernel_common (:514), call cuKernelGetName after cuFuncGetName fails.
findings.fix_risk:
(1) Once handles are named, every default-flag CUDA 13 binary gets redirected. In a stripped one, __constant__ and __device__ writes cannot be mirrored (same resolver). Without guard (d), the patched kernel would run on stale globals and give silently wrong results; krs-vec_add_legacy_fs shows that outcome (20 events, C[1]=0.00).
(2) cuKernelGetName must see only real handles. The dladdr==0 test excludes host stubs inside loaded objects, but host code in anonymous JIT memory would be misclassified, so the call has to fail cleanly (experiment a).
(3) Cached pointer->name entries must be dropped on __cudaUnregisterFatBinary or library unload, and in reset_late_bootstrap_state_for_next_attach (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1945), because addresses get reused.
(4) Launching in a context other than the one holding the patched module (non-primary context, another device) fails. The existing fallback at :215-231 relaunches the original; keep it.
(5) Rejecting size-0 entries loses assembly functions that lack .size. Compiler-generated CUDA stubs always have a size.

The alternative carries extra risk: it depends on cudart calling the exported cuLaunchKernel, and cu_launch_kernel_common passes a failed patched launch's error back to the application (:524, no fallback).

findings.root_cause:
(1) The preloaded agent initializes inside the main() wrapper (agent.cpp:561-581, the same in official/master). By then the executable's static constructors have already made their __cudaRegisterFunction and __cudaRegisterVar calls, so the registration-keyed map, the one route that needs no symbols, is empty.
(2) The late path can name a host address only from symbol tables:
- dladdr reads .dynsym. An executable puts only imports there unless linked with export-dynamic, and CUDA 13 marks __global__ host stubs HIDDEN, so not even then.
- The .symtab cache is gone after strip.
This part does not depend on CUDA 13: any stripped executable fails.
(3) The driver-level fallback (cuFuncGetName) did not rescue the launch either, most likely because cudart again passes a CUkernel handle.

All three misses are logged at DEBUG only. Shipped binaries normally have no .symtab: Debian/Ubuntu packaging moves it into -dbgsym packages. So this is the common case, not an edge case.
findings.fix_sketch:
Get symbol-free names from the registration calls, the same way the agent already interposes __cudaRegisterFatBinary (agent.cpp:840-856, exported in agent.version). That interposer demonstrably runs before main: the first line of every agent client.log, 'VM factory for name: llvm already registered, overwriting', is agent.cpp:850 running from the victim's static constructor, before 'Entered bpftime_agent_main'.

(1) Export interposers for __cudaRegisterFunction and __cudaRegisterVar from the agent (add both to agent.version). Forward through dlsym(RTLD_NEXT), and record hostFun->deviceName and hostVar->deviceName in a mutex-guarded, process-local table built on first use (safe before main).
(2) resolve_host_function_symbol (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1634) and mirror_cuda_memcpy_to_symbol (:1291) consult the table before dladdr and ELF. deviceName is already the device symbol, for example 'd_N', so no demangling is needed.
(3) Look up the Frida listener targets for these two functions with dlsym(RTLD_NEXT), as nv_attach_impl.cpp:369-372 already does for __cudaRegisterFatBinary, so the listeners stay on libcudart and not on the new interposers.
(4) Attach mode, where registration is long past and the table is empty:
- Name kernels with cudaFuncGetName (CUDA >= 12.3), once per pointer. Its header (cuda_runtime_api.h:4051-4074) says it names a registered entry-function pointer and treats any other pointer as a cudaKernel_t.
- Keep the F2 guard: a cudaMemcpyToSymbol(Async) target that cannot be named sets a flag and stops redirection with a WARN, so a patched kernel never runs on unmirrored globals.

Full attach-mode support for variables can come later: match cudaGetSymbolAddress(host var) against cuModuleGetGlobal of the original module (via cudaGetFuncBySymbol and cuFuncGetModule) for each global the PTX declares.
findings.fix_risk:
- Interposing changes the binding of every CUDA library's registrations (cuBLAS and others: thousands of entries), at a small memory and start-up cost.
- Libraries with statically linked cudart, and the dlmopen-ed agent of the syscall-trace transformer, are not interposed and keep today's paths.
- Entries must be erased on __cudaUnregisterFatBinary, because an unloaded library's hostFun addresses can be reused.
- cudaFuncGetName is a runtime call: a failure sets the runtime's last error, which an application checking cudaGetLastError() after <<<>>> would see. Call it once per pointer and clear only an error it produced: peek first, and reset only if the prior state was success. It does not exist before CUDA 12.3, so look it up with dlsym.
- The guard may turn off instrumentation for programs that write symbols no patched kernel reads. That is acceptable because it warns.
- The fix covers variables only in preload mode until the full mirror exists.

findings.root_cause: Since #695 (831caa95) the host-symbol cache keeps STT_NOTYPE (nv_elf_introspect.cpp:153-155; the comment justifies only STT_OBJECT). On AArch64 that admits the mapping symbols $x/$d (NOTYPE, size 0), which the assembler places at the start of every input section; with -fdata-sections _ZL3d_N starts its own .bss section, so $d has its address, and with -ffunction-sections the host wrapper _Z9vectorAddPKfS0_Pf shares its address with $x. Ties are not broken: both sorts compare only start (unstable std::sort twice), the resolver returns the last equal-start entry, and size-0 entries skip the range check (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1664-1674). Here resolve_host_function_symbol(&d_N) returned '$d', no module exports '$d', and mirror_cuda_memcpy_to_symbol returned silently, leaving the patched module's d_N at 0. The same mechanism threatens the launch: if $x ends last at 0x2500 the log says 'resolved $x but no patched CUfunction is registered', the original kernel runs, there are 0 events and C[1] = 3.00 (silent loss of instrumentation instead of wrong results). In this run the function won by luck of the global sort, not by design. mirror_cuda_memcpy_from_symbol has the same exposure (a '$d' name falls back to the original module, returning stale values).

If NOTYPE must stay for some reason, skip mapping symbols instead: 'if (type == STT_NOTYPE && sym.st_size == 0 && name[0] == '$') continue;'. (2) Make ties deterministic and prefer sized symbols in both sorts (nv_elf_introspect.cpp:175-178 and nv_attach_impl.cpp:1623-1626): 'return a.start != b.start ? a.start < b.start : (a.end - a.start) < (b.end - b.start);' so the sized entry sorts last and upper_bound/--it returns it. findings.what_i_checked:
Run data: 33 of 36 run dirs record server_rc=139 in meta.txt. That includes all 10 no-agent runs (krs-noagent, cc-noagent, m-A-noagent-r1..5, m-B-noagent-r1..3) and m-C-strace. hmt-legacy shows server_rc=124 because the harness timeout fired first, but its server.log says 'timeout: the monitored command dumped core'. That line ends 34 server.logs, and logs/meas.out prints 'Segmentation fault ... libbpftime-syscall-server.so' for every m-* run. th-ipc stopped early on map creation (CUDA IPC error 801), so it has no rc. runs/gdb-server-exit/gdb.log matches the claimed chain frame for frame, and the line numbers match the dev source: syscall_server_main.cpp:453 (close), syscall_context.cpp:280 (bpftime_close(fd)), handler_manager.cpp:118 (map_binding_guard), array_map_binding.hpp:23; fault in pthread_mutex_lock(0xffffe81d0078) = segment_manager 0xffffe81d0010 + 0x68.
How the shm is destroyed: through no __cxa_atexit object. It is an ELF destructor, `static __attribute__((destructor(65535))) void __destruct_shm()` (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:98 dev, :90 master). It calls bpftime_destroy_global_shm (:65; it sets global_shm_released at :73, then runs ~bpftime_shm at :75). readelf: the .fini_array of libbpftime-syscall-server.so is {__do_global_dtors_aux 0x7a5640, __destruct_shm 0x781a60}. _dl_call_fini runs that array from the end, so __destruct_shm runs first in that DSO. The only other exit hook is std::atexit(remove_syscall_server_global_shm) (syscall_server_utils.cpp:169), which only unlinks and never unmaps. The order between the two DSOs comes from _dl_fini's dependency sort: libbpftime-syscall-server.so has DT_NEEDED libcuda.so.1 (/opt/nvidia/l4t-gpu-libs/nvgpu), which has DT_NEEDED libnvrm_mem.so. Dependents are finalized before their dependencies, so the server's __destruct_shm runs before libnvrm_mem's destructor.
libnvrm_mem.so disassembly: its fini_array entry 0x2050 branches to 0x23d0, which runs `bl close@plt` at 0x2428. The return address 0x242c matches gdb frame #18 0xffffec33242c (base 0xffffec330000). The fd it closes was opened by NvRmMemMgrInit (0x24a4) as open64("/dev/nvmap", O_CLOEXEC), and the close is guarded by an init flag. So the close only happens after cuInit, which the server always calls: start_up -> ctx.initialize_cuda() at syscall_server_utils.cpp:178.
Use after destroy in dev: the disassembly of ~bpftime_shm (0x8288d0) only releases segment_owner, a shared_ptr. The disposer _Sp_counted_ptr_inplace<managed_shared_memory>::_M_dispose (0x837510) is just munmap/shmdt. It has no store that clears mp_header or m_base, because the compiler drops stores to an object whose lifetime is ending (lifetime dead-store elimination). The control block is then freed. So `segment` becomes a dangling reference to freed heap whose stale mp_header (0xffffe81d0010) points into the unmapped segment. That is exactly the gdb picture.

findings.root_cause:
Use of the destroyed global shm from the syscall server's close() interposer during a later library's ELF destructor. At exit, _dl_fini finalizes libbpftime-syscall-server.so before its dependencies libcuda.so.1 and libnvrm_mem.so. Its .fini_array runs __destruct_shm -> bpftime_destroy_global_shm, which sets global_shm_released and runs ~bpftime_shm: the shared segment is unmapped. bpftime_shm.manager stays a stale pointer into the old segment, and in dev `segment` becomes a dangling reference into a freed shared_ptr control block.
Then libnvrm_mem.so's destructor closes the /dev/nvmap fd that cuInit opened. The call reaches the preloaded close(). call_with_context only checks ctx_initialized==2, and syscall_context lives in a union that is never destroyed, so handle_close's guards (enable_mock, initializing_cuda, enable_mock_after_initialized) are all still true. bpftime_close(9) -> close_fd -> manager->clear_id_at(9, segment) touches unmapped memory and gets SIGSEGV. In dev it faults on map_binding_mutex(segment) at handler_manager.cpp:118; master would fault at handler_manager.cpp:100.
Nothing on this path consults global_shm_released, even though dev already sets it before the unmap. The hazard is not CUDA-specific (any destructor that runs after the server DSO and calls close() triggers it); CUDA makes it happen on every run.

  if (!initialize_ctx() || bpftime::global_shm_released.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) return fallback();
(plus #include "bpftime_shm_internal.hpp"). After __destruct_shm, every interposed call (close, mmap/mmap64, munmap, ioctl, epoll_*, open/openat, read, fopen, syscall/bpf) then goes straight to libc. A guard only in bpftime_close fixes the observed crash but leaves the mmap64-with-fd, epoll, dup3, perf-ioctl and bpf paths exposed.
findings.fix_risk: Low. findings.root_cause:
bootstrap_existing_fatbins() ingests fatbins from two overlapping sources without deduplication. The `.nv_fatbin` section pass reads from the section start through every contiguous blob (read_fatbin_bytes_from_ptr walks consecutive headers). Each `.nvFatBinSegment` wrapper's data pointer lands inside that same run in nvcc single-TU executables (the single wrapper -> blob1; the device-link wrapper -> the section start). The same PTX therefore goes through extract_ptxs, hack_fatbin and compile_ptxs 2 times (1 wrapper) or 3 times (2 wrappers) per bootstrap round.
The sha256-keyed patch, PTX and module caches turn the repeats into hits: no extra LLVM patch, ptxas compile, cuModuleLoadDataEx or device memory. The waste is one cuobjdump fork+exec with temp files, two hardware_concurrency thread pools, JSON plus SHA-256 hashing of the full PTX, and a duplicate fatbin_record kept in fatbin_records (about 1 KB of PTX text here). That is about 6.6 ms per redundant ingestion on the Orin.
Two-hook case: the whole bootstrap reruns once per added hook, so the redundant ingestions multiply by the number of rounds (cc/hmt 2 redundant of 4; cg 4 redundant of 6). The rerun's own extra real patch, compile and load, and the stale first module set, are F4 (#708), not this finding.

findings.root_cause: The ~1.06 ms per call comes from the watcher's unconditional std::this_thread::sleep_for(1ms) at the bottom of every iteration (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:275-276). After the watcher sets flag2 it sleeps 1 ms, plus ~50 us timer slack and the wakeup, before it reads flag1 again. The GPU posts the next request a few us after flag2, so every request waits one full sleep period. Serialization is real and covers the whole process: there is one request slot (CommSharedMem), one watcher thread, and one device-global spin lock taken lane by lane in a 32-lane loop (default_trampoline.cu:138-170). So all host calls of all threads, warps and blocks run one at a time. But serialization itself costs only ~5-6 us per call on this board (hsmulti control), under 1% of the 1.06 ms. Consequence: a launch takes at least threads x host calls x 1.06 ms. cc-legacy: 10 threads x 10 calls = 106 ms. A 1M-thread kernel with one printk per thread would take ~18.5 min per launch.
findings.fix_risk: One CPU core busy-polls while a helper-heavy kernel runs. This is bounded by the window after the last request; idle behaviour does not change. The plain `flag1 == 1` read must become an atomic or volatile acquire load. Today the opaque sleep_for call keeps the compiler from hoisting that load; in a spin loop without it, the compiler may turn the loop into an infinite one. Response writes must stay ordered before flag2: keep the seq_cst fence or use a release store. The fix does not touch the payload race, which stays as reachable as before. The DEBUG log lines (2 per request) become a visible part of the per-call cost.

Where 16464 comes from: llvmbpf's GPU lowering reserves a fixed stack of 32 bpf-to-bpf call frames x 512 B + 80 B (compiler.cpp:42-45, 396-402) for every program, whether or not it has local calls. The allocation disappears only if LLVM can delete or promote it; the empty probe never touches the stack, so it gets 0 B. As soon as a stack address escapes (passed to a helper, which almost every probe does; here 503/505 receive pointers to the &ev fields) or is indexed dynamically, the whole [2058 x i64] array stays. So the sampling probe gets 16464 B per thread and touches 56 B of it (0.34%).
Reservation: the driver must back this frame for every resident thread: 16464 B x 1536 x 8 SMs ~= 202 MB (193 MiB) of the shared DRAM while the patched module is in use. With one frame (592 B) it would be ~7.3 MB.
Occupancy is not affected. Registers rise from 12 to 28 (38 for threadscheduling), but at 256 threads per block at most 40 allocated registers x 1536 threads fit in 65536. Local memory is off-chip.
The data do not split the +410 us. Rough static bounds:
- +72 instructions x 32768 warps = 2.36 M warp-instructions, at least ~72 us at 32.6 G warp-instructions/s (8 SMs x 4 schedulers x 1.02 GHz).
- 19 local accesses of 8 B per thread = 38 L1 wavefronts per warp, ~150 us at one wavefront per SM per cycle.
So work per thread plausibly explains a large share: the zero-init written in the probe source, helper writes through generic pointers, reloads, two calls. An effect of the frame size itself is only a hypothesis: with the usual warp-interleaved local-memory layout, each warp slot's 56 touched bytes sit in a different ~527 KB slab, 48 slabs per SM, which strains TLB reach.
The llvm-jit submodule commit (87bac39) is the same on official/master.

What builds the cache: nv_attach_impl::build_host_symbol_cache_once (attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:1605-1632). It walks elf_introspect::list_loaded_modules (nv_elf_introspect.cpp:191-208), which uses dl_iterate_phdr and so sees every module of the base namespace; the dlmopen'ed pass libraries are not visible. It reads .symtab and .dynsym of each module into one sorted vector of {start, end, std::string}.
When: it is called eagerly from bootstrap_existing_fatbins_once (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1929-1933), called by start_late_bootstrap_async (1953-1981), called when the nv attach is registered (nv_attach_impl.cpp:228). Despite its name, start_late_bootstrap_async runs synchronously ('Run bootstrap in the caller thread'), so all of this happens during agent init, before the victim's main.
What it is for: only resolve_host_function_symbol (1634-1675), the fallback after dladdr. It is called from the late-attach launch path (nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:203) and from the __constant__/__device__ mirror paths (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1298, frida_setup.cpp:790) to name host stub and shadow-variable addresses. other_observations: Request payload race in the GPU->host bridge (code identical on official/master; PR #503 does not touch it). The helpers copy key, value, fmt and args into the single shared `req` before make_helper_call takes __bpftime_comm_lock (default_trampoline.cu:241-245, 298-305, 317-320, 330-339, 417-425). All lanes write at the same time, and each lane then sends whatever payload is in the slot. Evidence: the hmt-legacy client.log prints 'Thread (0,0,0)' for all 120 printk lines (10 threads x 2 x 6 launches). The ts-legacy server.log shows 1 thread-mapping entry instead of 10, and 51 threads in the SM histogram instead of 60 (9 NOEXIST updates per new key are lost). Fix: copy the payload inside the lock, e.g. by passing it into make_helper_call. Test: a 32-thread kernel doing printk or map updates with per-thread keys must produce 32 distinct values.

__bpftime_comm_lock is a .global in the trampoline PTX (trampoline_ptx.h:19), so every patched CUmodule has its own lock, while the request slot (constData -> CommSharedMem) is shared by the whole process. Concurrent kernels from two patched modules (e.g. two .cu files, or two streams) can therefore interleave on one slot. Found by reading; not exercised in these runs.

llvmbpf bpf-to-bpf calls move r10 by STACK_SIZE = 64, which is a slot count, used as a byte offset (vm/llvm-jit/src/compiler.cpp:1454-1461, and the return at :547-554). A callee's frame therefore starts 64 B below the caller's r10 and overlaps the caller's frame when the caller uses more than 64 B of stack. This affects both the CPU and GPU JIT in non-kernel-compatible mode; none of the GPU examples here use local calls. Test: main stores a sentinel at r10-128, calls a subprog that writes r10-8 to r10-64 of its own frame, then checks the sentinel.

default_trampoline.cu:21 sets GPU_HELPER_MAX_BUF = 1<<24, but the checked-in trampoline_ptx.h was generated with 1<<20: it reads resp at offset 2097184 = 24 + 2*(1<<20) + 8 (trampoline_ptx.h:122), which matches the host value 1<<20 (bpf_attach_ctx.hpp:43). Regenerating the PTX from the .cu as written would break the layout. PR #503 changes the .cu to 1<<20.

The late bootstrap ingests the same fatbin twice: once via .nv_fatbin (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1824-1849) and once via the .nvFatBinSegment wrapper that points into it (1851-1881). The log says 'ingested 2 fatbin(s)' and 'Prefilled patched CUDA kernel' appears twice; cuobjdump runs twice (~5 ms more start-up) and two fatbin_records are created.

start_late_bootstrap_async (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1953-1981) runs synchronously in the caller thread. The whole bootstrap (symbol cache, cuobjdump, patching, ptxas, module load) therefore sits on the victim's start-up path before main.

resolve_host_function_symbol's nearest-symbol lookup accepts zero-size entries without an end check (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1670-1674), and the cache keeps AArch64 $x/$d mapping symbols (~43% of entries). This is the mechanism behind the #646 kind of misresolution.

findings.fix_sketch: (A) Smallest change, recommended. In map_handler.cpp map_init, cases 1502 and 1503 (:1291-1341): if a cached probe says IPC is unusable (CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_INTEGRATED==1, or a one-time cuIpcGetMemHandle on a 2 MiB cuMemAlloc returns 801), set this->type to 1512/1513 and construct nv_gpu_array_host_map_impl / nv_gpu_shared_array_host_map_impl. Pass get_thread_count(attr) so the env override keeps working. Every dispatch already keys off `type` and already handles 1512/1513: lookup :251-290, update :561-600, delete :716-750, next_key :891-925, map_free ~:1547-1575, get_gpu_map_max_thread_count :1612, get_gpu_map_extra_buffer :1653, value size :94-96. create_map_basic_info (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:361) passes the new type to the GPU, whose trampoline already has the 1512/1513 paths, so the PTX does not change. For 1501: make nv_gpu_shared_hash_map_impl's value store pluggable (a template, or a member of type nv_gpu_shared_array_host_map_impl), add a host type id such as 1511 (GPU_MAP_OFFSET+HASH+10) and its dispatch cases. The device reaches 1501 through host calls anyway (_bpf_helper_ext_0001 has no 1501 fast path), so no PTX change there either. Lookups would then return a pointer into the registered segment, which also fixes the current behaviour of returning a copy. Along the way, add cuMemFree before the throws (nv_gpu_per_thread_array_map.cpp:76-81, nv_gpu_shared_array_map.cpp:55-62) and restore set_enable_mock(true) when a constructor throws. (B) Alternative: cuMemCreate with POSIX_FD handles plus cuMemExportToShareableHandle in the server, and cuMemImportFromShareableHandle + cuMemAddressReserve/cuMemMap/cuMemSetAccess in try_initialize_for_agent_and_get_mapped_address (per-thread map :17-46, shared map :247-374), with granularity rounding and cleanup. This needs a new channel to pass the fd: SCM_RIGHTS over a Unix socket, because pidfd_getfd is blocked here by Yama ptrace_scope=1 unless the server calls prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER). It keeps device-memory caching but is untested on nvgpu (only the attribute says 1) and is far bigger. Examples unblocked by A: 1502->1512 unblocks threadhist (and faiss/llama/pytorch-test, which have other blockers); 1503->1513 unblocks atomizer, mem_trace, launchlate, cutlass/counter and directly_run_on_gpu (the last also needs the bpftimetool direct run, see P-h); a 1501 host variant unblocks threadscheduling_dynamic_hook, and gpu_shared_map needs both 1503 and 1501. Unchanged: launchlate-kernel-gpu-shared-map and threadhist-gpu-kernel-shared-map (1504; they need root and a kernel map). Already IPC-free: cuda-counter, cudagraph, threadscheduling, kernel_trace, kernelretsnoop, host_map_test.
findings.corrections: (1) The message 'Unable to open CUDA IPC handle' is printed when cuIpcGetMemHandle fails in the server; nothing is being opened. (2) The line 'Unable to allocate map 1502 (Invalid argument)' comes from a dev-branch try/catch in map_init (map_handler.cpp:1042-1061, commit bf1af650). official/master has no catch there: the exception reaches handle_exceptions in syscall_server_main.cpp ('bpftime syscall interposer failed: ...'), which falls back to the real bpf() syscall. The example fails either way. (3) The survey's upstream reader listed kernelretsnoop among the IPC-blocked examples. It uses only 1527; the 1502 macro at kernelretsnoop.bpf.c:6 is defined but unused. The README list is correct, and the krs-* runs confirm it.
findings.fix_risk: A: low to moderate. The type reported back changes (BPF_OBJ_GET_INFO returns 1512, not 1502), which only matters to libbpf map reuse and pinning. GPU accesses go to host-pinned memory instead of device memory: the same DRAM on Orin, but cached differently, so per-thread counter cost should be measured with meas.sh. B: high.
findings.test_idea: On the board, rerun th-ipc with the same meta. Before: 'Unable to allocate map 1502'. After: the loader runs and its per-thread histogram for vec_add_legacy 10 5 10 1 shows 6 calls for each of threads 0-9. Mutation: force the IPC path (revert, or an env switch) and th-ipc fails again. CPU-only: factor out bpf_map_type pick_gpu_map_backend(requested, ipc_ok) and unit-test (1502,false)->1512, (1503,false)->1513, (1502,true)->1502.
findings.upstream: No issue or PR covers IPC-free 1501/1502/1503 (the survey's upstream reader: no PR addresses IPC-free GPU maps for Orin). PR #522 added 1512/1513 'for Tegra platforms without CUDA IPC'. Issue #488 (closed) was a different IPC error, 201.

findings.what_i_checked: nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:117-188 compiles inside boost::asio::post lambdas, which throw at :145 ('Unable to create nv_attach_impl_ptx_compiler') and :164 ('Unable to compile'). /usr/include/boost/asio/impl/thread_pool.ipp:32-44 (Boost 1.83): thread_function wraps scheduler run() in catch(...) { std::terminate(); }. hack_fatbin (nv_attach_impl.cpp:895-1076) uses the same pool pattern. The catch in bootstrap_existing_fatbins_once (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1935-1939) cannot see exceptions raised on pool threads. On the early path, try_loading_ptxs runs inside Frida listeners (nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:297 and :329), so even a cuModuleLoadDataEx failure (nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:237) would unwind through C frames and terminate. official/master is identical. No run hit this: every compile succeeded (krs-legacy: 'Compile of patched.temp.1.sm_75.ptx done').
findings.root_cause: Triage. Likely real on this board: yes, for real applications. Matters for users: yes, it kills the traced app with SIGABRT where running it unpatched would be the right outcome. Mechanism: exceptions thrown inside Boost thread-pool handlers or Frida callbacks are never caught. Triggers that exist here: any PTX that nvPTXCompiler 13.2 refuses for sm_87. That includes the sm_61 fallback (gpu-env/ptxprobe.out.txt: 'Value sm_61 is not defined for option gpu-name'); PTX with .version < 7.4, because rewrite_ptx_target only bumps .version for sm >= 100 (nv_attach_utils.cpp:32; llc15.ptxas.txt: 'PTX .version 7.1 does not support .target sm_87'); and library PTX built for newer GPUs, such as cuBLAS's sm_120-only PTX (P-j).
findings.fix_sketch: In both pool lambdas, wrap the body in try/catch, store the first std::exception_ptr under the existing mutex, and rethrow it on the calling thread after pool.join(). Better still, mark that PTX as failed and keep the original module. Wrap the try_loading_ptxs calls in the Frida listeners (frida_setup.cpp:297, :329) in try/catch: log an error and leave the fatbin unpatched, so launches use the original kernel.

findings.what_i_checked: bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:121-126 reads flag1 with a plain load, writes flag1 = 0, then reads request_id, map_id and req with plain loads; only the response side has seq_cst fences (:270-273). Disassembly of the built agent (CAND/build-cuda/runtime/agent/libbpftime-agent.so, watcher lambda at 0x8e35c0): 'ldr w1,[x0]; cmp w1,#1; b.eq' and then 'str wzr,[x0]; ldr x28,[x0,#16]; ldr w25,[x0,#12]'. There is no ldar or dmb between the flag load and the payload loads, and ARMv8 does not order loads behind a control dependency. The GPU side issues membar.sys before storing flag1 (trampoline_ptx.h:516-521). official/master is identical; open PR #503 adds exactly an acquire fence after the flag check, plus volatile fields. A bigger defect in the same protocol, confirmed by run data: every helper that sends a payload writes it into the single CommSharedMem.req before taking the lock, with all active lanes writing at the same moment. Sites: default_trampoline.cu:241-245 (lookup), :298-305 (update), :317-320 (delete), :331-341 (printk), :421-427 (puts). make_helper_call (:131-173) serializes lanes and takes __bpftime_comm_lock only after that. trampoline_ptx.h confirms it: the key-copy loops at :448 and :471 (st.u8 to constData+24) come before the lane loop at :496 and the atom.global.cas at :508-510. _bpf_helper_ext_0002 likewise stores key, value and flags (+2097176) before its CAS. Evidence: in /home/jetson/src/results/gpu/examples-20261109/runs/ts-legacy (threadscheduling, key = (block_x<<16)|thread_x, vec_add_legacy 10 5 10 1, so 6 launches of 10 threads), client.log has 60 'Executing map update for 3, result = 0' (fd 3 is thread_mapping). Yet server.log:363-366 'Thread-to-Hardware Mapping Samples' (which prints up to 10 entries) lists exactly one: Block (0,0,0) Thread (0,0,0) Warp 1 Lane 0. If each lane sent its own payload there would be 10 keys, and lane 9, served last, would own the final write. The lookup keys in these examples are the same across a warp (pid, SM id), which is why the cc-legacy and ts histograms look correct.
findings.root_cause: Triage. (1) Missing acquire on the host: real at the ISA level but rare in practice. flag1, request_id and map_id sit in one cache line, the GPU fences with membar.sys, and the host polls every 1 ms. The impact would be serving a stale operation or key. Also, std fences emit dmb ish; formally a device observer needs outer-shareable ordering. Whether that matters on Tegra234 is uncertain. (2) Payload race: real and observed on this board. Matters for users: yes. Any GPU program whose host-call map update, delete or lookup keys (or printk arguments) differ between lanes silently gets wrong data. Underlying causes: the payload is staged in a shared buffer outside the critical section, and the lock is a per-module __device__ variable (trampoline_ptx.h:19), so the protocol is not serialized across patched modules either.
findings.fix_sketch: Host side: 'if (__atomic_load_n(&m->flag1, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == 1)' and '__atomic_store_n(&m->flag2, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)'; PR #503's fence is equivalent for the first. Device side: have make_helper_call take the payload (key/value pointers and sizes, flags, or a copy callback) and copy it into req after spin_lock and before 'membar.sys; st flag1'. Move the lock word into CommSharedMem and take it with atom.sys.cas so all modules share one lock; the survey verified a CAS lock in host memory works here (gpu-env/hostreg.atom-dual.txt: counter=1600 expected=1600). Regenerate trampoline_ptx.h with GPU_HELPER_MAX_BUF = 1<<20 (see P-k).
findings.corrections: The claim names only the missing acquire. The host-call bug that actually bites on this board is the payload being written outside the lock, by all lanes at once; ts-legacy shows it.
findings.experiment_needed: Payload race, a stronger repro: the ts-legacy setup with vec_add_legacy 64 2 32 2. Expected now: thread_mapping has about 2 entries (one per warp) instead of 64. The acquire issue is not cheaply observable; it would need a stress run with lane-uniform but per-launch-changing keys, compared against a ground truth.
findings.fix_risk: Medium. The trampoline PTX must be regenerated (the Makefile expects clang++-17; this board has LLVM 15/16). The critical section grows because the copy happens under the lock. Any CommSharedMem layout change has to be mirrored in runtime/include/bpf_attach_ctx.hpp.
findings.test_idea: On the board, rerun ts-legacy: before the fix, 1 thread_mapping entry; after, 10 (keys 0..9, each with its own lane id). With 64 2 32 2: 64. Mutation: move the copy back in front of the lock and it drops to 1 entry per warp. CPU-only guard: parse trampoline_ptx.h and require that inside _bpf_helper_ext_0002 the first store to constData+24 comes after the lock CAS (fails on today's file).
findings.upstream: PR #503 (open, last updated 2026-08-09) covers only the fence and volatile fields. The payload race is not tracked in any of the survey's dumps. Closed issue #486 ('BPF map consistency ... multiple thread blocks') may be related; I did not read it. The per-lane loop came with #413 (633edde4, 2025-07), and the payload copy has stayed outside it since.

findings.what_i_checked: default_trampoline.cu:359-411 and the PTX actually shipped (trampoline_ptx.h:1373-1540). In order: 'st.u32 [hdr+16],1' (dirty=1); 'atom.add.u64 [hdr+8],1' (relaxed, gpu scope: the __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST was lowered without fences); plain st.u8 data copy; 'st.u32 [hdr+16],0'. There is no membar or fence anywhere in the function. Host side, drain_data (nv_gpu_ringbuf_map.cpp:56-81): one acquire fence before the loop, which orders nothing that follows; then plain reads of dirty, head, tail, the size field and the data. head is advanced (:71) before fn() reads the slot. The function returns at the first dirty header (:64-66). The server reaches it through bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1580-1598. In the runs (krs-legacy, krs-geom, kt-legacy) the events look sane and 'Ignored dirty pages' never appears, but those runs had at most 7 threads and 6 launches.
findings.root_cause: Triage. Likely real on this board: yes under load; invisible in the tiny runs. Matters for users: kernel_trace and kernelretsnoop users can get torn or garbage events, with a garbage size passed to the user callback because size is not checked against value_size, and silent drops: the early return starves later headers, and a full ring returns 2. Mechanism: the protocol is unsound even under sequential consistency. The reader sees dirty==0; the writer then sets dirty=1 and bumps tail; the reader sees the new tail and consumes a slot not yet written. Without system-scope fences the CPU can also see tail++ (and dirty=0) before the data stores.
findings.fix_sketch: GPU side: reserve the slot with atom.add on tail, write the payload, execute fence.sc.sys (membar.sys), then publish with st.release.sys of a per-slot commit word = seq+1, or of a separate committed tail. Host side: load the commit word with ldar before reading the slot, read the payload, then store-release head. Skip only the header being written instead of returning from the whole drain, and clamp size to value_size.

If real: invalid or torn records above zero, and/or many 'Ignored dirty pages'. If not: zero over more than 1e7 records, which still does not prove absence.
findings.fix_risk: Moderate. The ring layout changes and the PTX must be regenerated.
findings.test_idea: A deterministic host-only unit test of nv_gpu_ringbuf_map_impl::drain_data. Construct the map in a test managed_shared_memory, write a header {head=0, tail=1, dirty=0} with the slot reserved but not committed (garbage size), call drain_data, and assert the callback is not invoked. Today it is invoked, so the test fails; it passes after the fix, and removing the commit check makes it fail again.

findings.what_i_checked: bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:140-185: the lookup result ptr goes to cuPointerGetAttribute(MEMORY_TYPE). Device or unified pointers are passed through unchanged. Anything else becomes comm_device_base + (ptr - comm_host_base), with no bounds check. That is only valid inside the cudaHostRegister'ed segment (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1416-1433 registers [segment base, size)). Pointers outside it exist: array_map_kernel_user.cpp:142 returns into a process-local mmap of a BPF_F_MMAPABLE kernel array, and kernel_map_local.cpp:30/65 returns thread_local buffers. gpu-env/hostreg.hostptr.txt shows that handing the GPU a host pointer ends in an illegal memory access (CAN_USE_HOST_POINTER_FOR_REGISTERED_MEM=0). Related: a host-call lookup on 1501 returns a pointer to nv_gpu_shared_array_map's single value_buffer copy (nv_gpu_shared_array_map.cpp:82-123), so device writes through it are lost.
findings.root_cause: Triage. Likely real on this board: latent. No runnable example does host-call lookups on maps whose values live outside the segment: they use BPF_MAP_TYPE_HASH stored in shm, and the kernel-shared examples use 1504's device fast path. Matters for users: moderate, for anyone mixing kernel maps with GPU probes. The failure is CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS, which is sticky and kills the victim's CUDA context. Mechanism: the host-to-device translation assumes every value pointer lies in the one registered segment.
findings.fix_sketch: Translate against the registered segment: if seg_lo <= p and p + value_size <= seg_hi, return seg_dev + (p - seg_lo). Otherwise set resp.value = nullptr and warn once, or copy the value into a staging slot inside CommSharedMem for read-only use.
findings.experiment_needed: Not cheap (needs root). A probe that calls bpf_map_lookup_elem on a kernel-user array map (bound to a BPF_F_MMAPABLE kernel array) from a kprobe on vectorAdd. Expected if real: the victim's cudaDeviceSynchronize returns 700, or garbage is read. Clean the root-owned /dev/shm segments afterwards.
findings.fix_risk: Low.
findings.test_idea: Factor out uintptr_t host_to_device(p, len, seg_lo, seg_len, seg_dev). Unit test: p outside the segment returns 0 (today a non-zero bogus pointer); p inside returns seg_dev + offset. Dropping the range check makes the test fail.

findings.what_i_checked: There is one CommSharedMem per segment, looked up by the name 'cuda_comm_shared_mem' (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1051-1069) and constructed by the server (:1071-1083). Every agent memsets it during init (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:393) and runs its own watcher thread polling the same flag1 (:121-123). GET_CURRENT_PID_TGID answers with the serving process's getpid()/gettid() (:244-253). The host-to-device pointer translation uses the serving agent's own mapping (:166-184). The GPU lock is per module and per process (trampoline_ptx.h:19). Per-thread HOST maps and 1527 are indexed by global thread id only (default_trampoline.cu:180-199, :365-380), so two processes share slots. Two processes can both register the same shm (gpu-env/hostreg.atom-dual.txt). No run had two victims.
findings.root_cause: Triage. Likely real on this board: yes, as soon as two victims make host calls at the same time. A later agent's memset can wipe flag1 of an in-flight request, and the GPU thread then spins on flag2 forever: the kernel hangs while holding the module lock. Both watchers can serve the same request (double map updates, wrong pid). A request served by the other agent gets a device pointer from the wrong context, which means an illegal address. Matters for users: yes, for multi-process GPU services traced by one server. It also applies inside one process when two patched module sets run concurrently (the kprobe+kretprobe sets of #708).
findings.fix_sketch: Give each process its own CommSharedMem: construct one per agent pid in the segment (named 'cuda_comm_shared_mem.<pid>'). constData is already set per process. Drop the memset of the shared object. Put the lock word in that per-process CommSharedMem and use system-scope atomics, so every module of a process serializes on it. Free it when the agent exits.
findings.experiment_needed: Cheap. Start one cuda-counter loader. Then start two victims on the same BPFTIME_GLOBAL_SHM_NAME, about 1 s apart: 'timeout 120 env LD_PRELOAD=CAND/build-cuda/runtime/agent/libbpftime-agent.so BPFTIME_SM_ARCH=sm_87 vec_add_legacy 1024 2000 256 4'. Control: the same two runs one after the other, giving the expected per-pid call_count. Expected if real: a victim hangs until timeout (rc 124), or a pid's count differs from the control or is credited to the other pid, or CUDA error 700. Run ps afterwards to check for leftovers.
findings.fix_risk: Low to moderate.
findings.test_idea: The two-victim run: before the fix, a hang or wrong counts; after, both exit 0 with per-pid counts equal to the control. Unit: two simulated agent pids get different CommSharedMem addresses; going back to a shared name gives the same address, so the test fails.

findings.what_i_checked: Only run_attach_entry_on_gpu passes the detected arch to LLVM (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1129-1141). The kprobe, kretprobe and memcapture passes hard-code 'sm_61', which LLVM 15 knows (ptxpass_kprobe_entry/main.cpp:55, ptxpass_kretprobe/main.cpp:43, ptxpass_kprobe_memcapture/main.cpp:141). gpu-env/llc15.out.txt: 'llc-15 -mcpu=sm_87' prints 'sm_87 is not a recognized processor for this target (ignoring processor)' and emits the header '.version 3.2 .target sm_87', which ptxas rejects (llc15.ptxas.txt). bpftime strips LLVM's header (filter_compiled_ptx_for_ebpf_program and filter_out_version_headers_ptx) and puts the trampoline's '.version 8.1' with the rewritten .target in front, so the expected result is a warning plus generic code generation. The direct run is reached through bpftimetool (tools/bpftimetool/main.cpp:364-368), and its example uses 1503 maps, which are blocked by F3.
findings.root_cause: Triage. Likely real on this board: the warning, yes; an actual failure is unlikely, because the header is replaced and eBPF code needs nothing beyond the generic subtarget. Matters for users: low (direct GPU run is a niche path, and on this board it is blocked by IPC anyway). Mechanism: llvmbpf is handed the real SM name only on this path, and LLVM 15's processor list stops at sm_86.
findings.fix_sketch: When LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR < 16, clamp the CPU name passed to LLVM to the highest one it knows that is at most the target (sm_86), since the header is replaced anyway. Or build llvmbpf against llvm-16-dev, which is installed here.

findings.what_i_checked: bootstrap_existing_fatbins (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1814-1906) walks every loaded module (elf_introspect::list_loaded_modules) and every .nv_fatbin section or .nvFatBinSegment wrapper, runs cuobjdump --extract-ptx once per fatbin (extract_ptxs), and calls try_loading_ptxs. hack_fatbin (:890-1076) emits every PTX file whether or not a pass changed it (ptx_out['patched.'+file] is set regardless of should_add_trampoline), and compile_ptxs plus try_loading_ptxs compile and cuModuleLoadDataEx all of them. A read-only ELF scan (my script /tmp/claude-2002/-home-jetson-src/6ac0883f-4479-466c-bec5-5fa31cffe4de/scratchpad/verify-buildipc/fatbin_walk.py): libcublas.so.13.4.1.3 has a 52 MiB .nv_fatbin and 193 wrappers; libcublasLt.so.13.4.1.3 has a 156 MiB .nv_fatbin and 2617 wrappers (each wrapper's walk covers 1-2 fatbins, so there is no quadratic copying); libcusparse has a 150 MiB .nv_fatbin. The survey's listings show 188 + 289 PTX files in cuBLAS/cuBLASLt, all sm_120. Upstream issue #552 measured 0.54 s per extraction and a 28 s first cold fatbin on an RTX 5090 host.
findings.root_cause: Triage. Likely real on this board: yes, for any victim that links cuBLAS, cuBLASLt or cuSPARSE. Agent start would run about 2,800 cuobjdump extractions (tens of minutes at about 0.5 s each), then compile about 480 sm_120 PTX files for sm_87; their .version is left as is, since rewrite_ptx_target only bumps it for sm >= 100. Compile errors are likely (sm_90+ and sm_120 instructions; unverified) and would abort the app through P-a. Matters for users: high. Also, with SPDLOG at debug level, hack_fatbin leaves a /tmp/bpftime-fatbin-work.* dump per fatbin (74 such directories exist in /tmp now). Mechanism: the late bootstrap does not filter by attach-point kernel and compiles unmodified PTX.
findings.fix_sketch: Drop PTX that no pass modified (should_add_trampoline == false): do not compile or load it, keep the original module; the launch path already falls back when there is no patched function. Before running cuobjdump on a fatbin, check its bytes or ELF symbol names for an attach-point kernel name and skip fatbins without one. Optionally scan only the main executable unless configured otherwise.

findings.what_i_checked: default_trampoline.cu:21 has GPU_HELPER_MAX_BUF = 1 << 24. runtime/include/bpf_attach_ctx.hpp:39-45 has BPFTIME_GPU_HELPER_MAX_BUF (1 << 20), with a comment that changing it requires regenerating trampoline_ptx.h. The PTX that ships uses the 1<<20 offsets: resp at +2097184 (trampoline_ptx.h:121, 529, 1065, 1193, 1291, 1364, 1626), map_update.value at +1048600 (:978, :1004), flags at +2097176 (:1016). These equal 24 + 2*2^20 + 8 and so on; with 1<<24, resp would be at +33554464, which does not appear. map_info[40960] = 1024 x sizeof(MapBasicInfo), which is 40 bytes (nv_attach_impl.hpp:45-53), so that matches too. History: the .cu's 1<<24 came with #514 (3f951f73, 2025-11-27); the host's 1<<20 and the regenerated PTX came with #542 (fac864e5, 2026-05-11), which left the .cu untouched.
findings.root_cause: Triage. Likely real on this board: latent; host and PTX agree at runtime today. Matters for users: for anyone who regenerates the trampoline, which the P-c fix requires. Running 'make -C attach/nv_attach_impl/trampoline' (its Makefile rewrites ../trampoline_ptx.h from the .cu) would produce PTX that reads resp 32 MiB past the end of the 2 MiB structure, so host-call results become garbage or an illegal address.
findings.fix_sketch: Set GPU_HELPER_MAX_BUF to 1 << 20 in default_trampoline.cu (PR #503 does exactly this). Better, put the layout in one header shared by the .cu and bpf_attach_ctx.hpp.
findings.fix_risk: Low.

Most important new defect: GPU host calls stage the key, value, flags and printk arguments in the single CommSharedMem.req before taking the lock, and every lane writes at the same time. default_trampoline.cu:241-245, 298-305, 317-320, 331-341 and 421-427; confirmed in trampoline_ptx.h:448-510. runs/ts-legacy shows it: 60 successful updates to thread_mapping left exactly 1 entry (thread 0, lane 0) where 10 were expected. Every probe with lane-dependent host-call keys gets wrong data silently. Details and fix under P-c.

Separate patched modules each have their own __bpftime_comm_lock (trampoline_ptx.h:19) but all point at the same CommSharedMem. So kernels from two patched modules running at once (two .cu files, or the kprobe+kretprobe module sets of #708) are not serialized against each other.

A 1501 (GPU hash) lookup through a host call returns a pointer to the single shared value_buffer copy (nv_gpu_shared_array_map.cpp:82-123, reached via nv_gpu_shared_hash_map.cpp:58). Writes through it never reach device memory, and concurrent lookups overwrite each other.

When a GPU map constructor throws: nv_gpu_per_thread_array_map.cpp:61-82 and nv_gpu_shared_array_map.cpp:42-63 leak the cuMemAlloc buffer (no cuMemFree before the throw). map_handler.cpp:1267/1292/1320 call set_enable_mock(false) and never restore it, and the dev branch's catch in map_init (:1042-1061) does not restore it either. Afterwards the loader's bpf() calls bypass bpftime.

Thread counts: 1512 is created with attr.gpu_thread_count (map_handler.cpp:1413-1420), while 1502 honours BPFTIME_MAP_GPU_THREAD_COUNT (:1306). get_value_size() (:94-96) always multiplies by attr.gpu_thread_count, so with the env var set a 1502 map's reported value size and its internal entry size disagree.

rewrite_ptx_target (nv_attach_utils.cpp:30-43) never raises .version for sm_87, which needs 7.4 or later, so PTX built by CUDA 11.3 or older fails to compile and aborts through P-a. For sm >= 100 it overwrites .version and can lower it. get_gpu_sm_arch also calls setenv inside the victim (:156).
Harness masking: scripts/run.sh:34 sets BPFTIME_SM_ARCH=sm_87 for every victim, so SM auto-detection never ran in this evaluation.
drain_data (nv_gpu_ringbuf_map.cpp:64-76) returns at the first dirty header, which starves the headers after it, and it advances head before reading the slot.
create_map_basic_info (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:340 versus :350) takes local_basic_info[i] before checking i < size. That is undefined behaviour when a map fd is 1024 or higher.

With debug logging, hack_fatbin's dumps of patched PTX (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1050-1066) are never removed; /tmp currently holds 74 bpftime-fatbin-work.* directories from these runs. I deleted nothing because this task was read-only.

overall: 1. On this board, nvcc 13.2's default launch path is never instrumented, so probes only work on victims rebuilt with -D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH -Xcompiler -D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH. krs-default gets 0 events vs krs-legacy's 20. The agent prints 'Attach successfully' and then logs, at DEBUG only, 'Late attach launch: resolved __end__ but no patched CUfunction is registered' for every launch. cg-vec_add_graph shows that only the cudaLaunchKernel path is affected: in the same process, the 5 cudaGraphLaunch kernels were instrumented (calls 1..5, 45 host calls = 5x9), because the v2 graph hook names the CUkernel with cuKernelGetName (nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:474-487 and the v2 params helper). The <<<>>> launch was missed; the legacy build counts 6. Root cause: cuda_launch_kernel_common (frida_setup.cpp:165-245) receives a CUkernel heap handle. symbol_address_to_fatbin is keyed by host stub, and resolve_host_function_symbol (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1635-1675) checks the end only when end>start (1670-1674), so a zero-size linker symbol matches any higher address and the heap pointer becomes __end__. The code is identical in official/master. Upstream: issue #646 (GB300, 'resolved _fini'), open, no PR. Fix: in the late path, if dladdr(func) finds no containing object, treat func as a CUkernel and name it with the existing cuKernelGetName helper before resolving symbols; let zero-size entries match only addr==start. Risk: low, since legacy stubs always live inside an ELF image and handles do not. Mutation-checkable tests: a GPU case running kernelretsnoop against a default-built vec_add 5 3 5 1 that expects 20 'Thread (' lines (0 today); a CPU unit test of the lookup on {__end__,0x2000,0x2000} that queries 0x5000 and expects nullopt (returns __end__ today).

2. Two probes on one kernel silently corrupt the traced program. cc-legacy and hmt-legacy (kprobe + kretprobe on vectorAdd) print Validation C[1] = 0.00 instead of 3.00. Without the agent (cc-noagent, krs-noagent), and in every single-probe run on the normal build, it is 3.00. Both logs contain 'new hook added after bootstrap; rerunning late bootstrap' and end with two patched PTX hashes. Path: nv_attach_impl.cpp:209-213 reruns bootstrap but keeps the first module set. record_patched_kernel_function (591-604) overwrites by name, so launches use the last set. mirror_cuda_memcpy_to_symbol (1323-1356) stops at the first module that exports d_N. So cudaMemcpyToSymbol(d_N) writes set A while the launched kernel in set B reads d_N=0. Upstream: issue #708 and PR #709, both open; the maintainer warned that the PR unloads modules without first waiting for in-flight launches. A smaller alternative: mirror into every patched module that exports the symbol (drop the break), and read memcpyFromSymbol from the set that launches use. Test: cuda-counter or host_map_test with vec_add_legacy 10 5 10 1, asserting C[1] = 3.00 (fails today).

3. On aarch64, a single probe can also silently corrupt __constant__ data. krs-vec_add_legacy_fs (victim built with -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections) gets all 20 events and the same patched PTX as krs-legacy, yet prints C[1] = 0.00. In that binary, _ZL3d_N (symtab #73) shares address 0x20040 with the mapping symbol $d (#85), and the host stub (#159) shares 0x2500 with $x (#61). nv_elf_introspect.cpp:148-171 keeps STT_NOTYPE $-symbols. The cache is sorted only by start address (std::sort at nv_elf_introspect.cpp:175 and nv_attach_impl.cpp:1623), and the lookup returns the last entry at the address. If ties keep symtab order, the stub resolves correctly (matching the log) and d_N resolves to $d. cuModuleGetGlobal then finds nothing, and mirror_cuda_memcpy_to_symbol returns without any log line (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1360). x86 has no mapping symbols, so upstream CI cannot see this. The survey critic predicted it; no upstream issue exists. Fix: skip $-prefixed and zero-size NOTYPE entries; on equal starts prefer sized FUNC/OBJECT symbols; warn when a symbol copy cannot be mirrored. Tests: a pure lookup unit test with {_ZL3d_N,0x1000,0x1004} and {$d,0x1000,0x1000} in both insertion orders, expecting _ZL3d_N; and the fs GPU run expecting 3.00. Experiment needed to prove which name the resolver returned (not run): in gdb, break on bpftime::attach::nv_attach_impl::resolve_host_function_symbol in the fs victim and 'finish' the call made from mirror_cuda_memcpy_to_symbol. If the $d tie is the cause, it returns '$d'; if it returns '_ZL3d_N', look at the copy itself. The control vec_add_legacy must return _ZL3d_N.

4. GPU-to-host helper calls lose per-thread arguments whenever several threads call them at once. make_helper_call serializes only the handshake, under __bpftime_comm_lock per lane (default_trampoline.cu:131-172). Each helper writes its payload into the single shared req union before calling it: lookup at 241-245, update 298-305, delete 317-320, printk 331-341, puts around 417-427. So every active lane overwrites the same buffer, and the lanes then submit it one after another. hmt-legacy: all 120 printk host calls carry arg1=0 (thread 0), while the per-thread host map in the same run holds thread ids 0..9. ts-legacy: thread_mapping took 60 successful updates but holds 1 key instead of 10. The code is identical in official/master. PR #503 only adds volatile and fences; PR #624 (open) adds a verifier that flags helpers called with different values per lane; no issue tracks the runtime bug. Fix: copy the payload after spin_lock inside make_helper_call (pass key/value pointers and sizes, or a fill lambda) and regenerate trampoline_ptx.h. Risk: moderate, since it touches every host-call helper and regenerated PTX; the host struct layout stays the same. Test: a kprobe calling bpf_map_update_elem(&hash,&tid,&tid,BPF_ANY) on a CPU HASH map with vec_add_legacy 32 1 32 1, asserting 32 keys (1 today); or ts-legacy expecting 10 samples.

5. Each GPU-to-host helper call costs about 1.05 ms. The agent's watcher sleeps 1 ms on every loop, even right after serving a request (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:122, 275-276; same in official). Three runs agree: cc-legacy, 610 calls over 6 launches -> median 106185.82 us per launch vs 35.20 us without the agent; hmt-legacy, 20 printk per launch -> 21273.54 us; ts-legacy, about 36 calls per timed launch -> mean 38163.83 us. One shared slot serializes every GPU thread, so a per-thread CPU-map or printk probe makes a kernel take (threads x calls) ms. The survey measured a spin-polled round trip of 4.9 us on this board, so the protocol itself is fast. Probes using only GPU-resident maps and helpers make no host calls. Fix: keep spinning (with yield) while requests keep arriving, and sleep only after an idle period. Risk: one CPU core busier while host calls are heavy. Test: one launch making 1000 bpf_get_current_pid_tgid calls must finish in under 0.1 s (about 1.05 s today).

6. The GPU ringbuf (map type 1527) drops events silently and delivers at most one event per thread slot per poll. In each m-B-sample run, 13 of 201 events arrived, stamped 0.59 ms apart: the first 13 launches. On the GPU, once tail-head reaches max_entries (16) the helper returns 2 and the event is gone (default_trampoline.cu:383-387). On the host, drain_data takes one entry per slot per call and returns early if any slot is dirty (nv_gpu_ringbuf_map.cpp:56-80); kernelretsnoop and kernel_trace poll once per second (krs-legacy shows one launch per poll). Here 185 events were dropped on the GPU and 3 were still buffered when the harness stopped the loader. Fix: drain every available entry per slot (loop until head==tail; skip dirty slots with continue instead of returning), and add a drop counter. Test: a host-only unit test that writes 5 entries into slot 0 of a SHM_REMOVE_AND_CREATE ringbuf and expects 5 callbacks from one drain_data call (1 today).

7. Start-up costs +1.61 s per traced CUDA process: m-A client_ms 1722-1742 with the agent vs 112-113 without; m-B 1765-1768 vs 154. m-C-strace attributes 1.39 s of it to build_host_symbol_cache_once (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1605-1632), which runs on the main thread before main(). Reading libbpftime-agent.so takes 0.73 s and libnv_attach_impl_ptx_compiler.so 0.61 s. Those two libraries supply about 538k of the 556,752 cached symbols; the victim supplies 100. nv_elf_introspect.cpp:139-146 does one seek+read per 24-byte symbol. The code is identical in official, and the RelWithDebInfo .symtab makes it worse. Fix: read each symbol table with one read or mmap, and index only modules that carry .nv_fatbin (or index lazily on first miss). Test: assert 'cached N host symbols' < 1000 for vec_add, or start-up < 0.3 s.

8. Every loader under libbpftime-syscall-server.so segfaults at exit on this board. server_rc is 139 in 33 of 34 runs; in hmt-legacy it is 124 because its own timeout fired, and that log still ends in 'dumped core'. It happens with no victim too (cc-noagent, krs-noagent, gdb-server-exit). gdb shows: _dl_fini -> libnvrm_mem.so destructor -> close(9) -> server close hook -> bpftime_close (syscall_context.cpp:280) -> clear_id_at (handler_manager.cpp:118) on a segment that __destruct_shm (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:98-120) had already unmapped. official/master reaches the same path (close_fd checks only the dangling `manager`). The dev branch's global_shm_released flag is not consulted there, and its map_binding_mutex only moves the faulting line. Collected events are not affected, but every loader exits with status 139. Fix: return to the original close once global_shm_released is set (in official: set manager to null in ~bpftime_shm). Test: init a global shm, call bpftime_destroy_global_shm(), then bpftime_close(3) (crashes today); plus a CI check that kernelretsnoop exits 0 after SIGINT. Experiment needed for official parity: rerun gdb-server-exit.sh against an official/master build. If official shares the bug, expect the same SIGSEGV in clear_id_at; if not, a clean exit.

9. Probe overhead, with clocks locked and info logging. An empty kprobe has no measurable cost on 5-thread launches (m-A medians 24.4-40.6 us vs 34.7-38.1 us, with bimodal noise) and costs +8% on 1M-thread launches (175.97 vs 162.31 us). The sampling probe costs 3.6x (585.59 us). Any probe whose stack address escapes gets a 16,464-byte per-thread stack frame (ptxas output for kernelretsnoop, kernel_trace-sample, host_map_test; the empty probe gets 0). The cause is llvmbpf's GPU stack, i64[64*32+10] (vm/llvm-jit/src/compiler.cpp:42-45, 396-402; same commit 87bac39 in official). At full occupancy that reserves about 193 MiB of local memory (16464 B x 1536 threads x 8 SMs). How much of the 3.6x comes from the frame is not isolated. Experiment needed: size the GPU stack to one frame and rerun m-B-sample three times. If the frame matters, the median falls well below 586 us; if the per-thread helper calls dominate, it stays within 5%. ptxas must then report at most 600 B.

10. What does work on Orin Nano with CUDA 13.2, for legacy-launch, unstripped victims and one probe: the kprobe_entry and kretprobe PTX passes, nvPTXCompiler from sm_75 PTX to sm_87, cuobjdump extraction, module load, host-registered shm, the globaltimer and thread/block index helpers, the 1527 ringbuf and the 1512/1513 host-backed GPU maps. Event counts match the launch geometry exactly: krs 20 = 4x5 and 21 = 3x7, kt-legacy 1 per launch, hmt 6 per key and 60 calls, cg 5 and 6 calls. The victim stays correct except in the configurations of items 2-3. The graph hooks already handle CUDA 13 handle launches.

11. Every failure above is silent at the default info level. Across all 33 agent logs, the only warnings are 24 'VM factory ... already registered' and 25 'Not a GPU map!' (the latter for the printk format-string array map, map type 2). 'Attach successfully' appears when nothing is instrumented (krs-default, stripped), and the wrong-result runs log nothing. Other limits: stripped victims are never instrumented; maps that need CUDA IPC fail (th-ipc: error 801); BPFTIME_SM_ARCH=sm_87 was forced in every run, so SM auto-detection was not exercised; bootstrap re-processes the same fatbin 2-3 times, and again on a second attach.

12. Caveats in the data. hmt-legacy and cc-legacy used run.sh before its 04:02 edit: the victim started 99.7 s after the loader, and hmt's loader was stopped by its own 120 s timeout. Medians from DEBUG runs include logging, and the krs runs predate the 04:15 clock lock, so only m-A, m-B and m-C count as timing evidence. kt-legacy's victim output was lost (buffered stdout, killed by SIGINT), so its correctness is unverified. Races in the example programs explain cuda-counter calls=51 and threadscheduling SM=51 / warps=24 instead of 60: 10 lanes insert the first key with BPF_NOEXIST at once. cuda-counter's 60 failed deletes use the wrong key (an example bug). The victim's 'GB/s' figures are MiB/s (benchmark_common.h:65-67).
